memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then they went to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal and said to him and the Israelites, "We have come from a distant country; make a treaty with us." The Israelites said to the Hivites, "But perhaps you live near us, so how can we make a treaty with you?" — Josh 9:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Gibeonites arrive with their carefully rehearsed story: "We have come from a distant country; make a treaty with us." And notice, to their credit, that the Israelites are initially cautious. They ask exactly the right question: "But perhaps you live near us?" There is a flicker of healthy suspicion here. Something did not quite add up, and Israel sensed it.

This is an important moment. The Israelites had good instincts. They knew God's instructions and rightly wondered whether these strangers might be local Canaanites in disguise. The warning signs were there, and they noticed them. The problem, as we will see, was not that they failed to ask the question. It was that they did not press the question far enough — all the way to God.

There is wisdom here for us. God often gives us discernment, a sense that something is not right. Those instincts are a gift, and we should not ignore them. When something feels off, that unease may be God's grace prompting us to look more closely and seek His guidance before we act.

The tragedy of this story is that Israel had the discernment but did not follow it through to prayer. How often we too sense a warning, ask a good question, and then rush ahead anyway without taking it to God. Scripture urges us, "If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God" (Jas 1:5). When we feel that flicker of doubt, the wisest thing we can do is pause and bring it to the Lord, who gives wisdom generously to all who ask.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you pay attention to the "flicker of doubt" God sometimes gives you?
2. When something feels off, do you press the question all the way to God in prayer?
3. Where might God be prompting you to slow down and seek His wisdom right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the discernment You give me. Help me not to ignore Your warnings but to bring my doubts and questions to You before I act. Amen.
